newsitem.title: GREECE: GREECE IS CONVERGING, FISCAL POLICY BALANCED - FINMIN.
newsitem.headline: GREECE IS CONVERGING, FISCAL POLICY BALANCED - FINMIN.

text.p: The nominal and real convergence of the Greek economy is proceeding smoothly, supported by a fiscal policy based both on spending cuts and tax collection, Deputy Finance Minister Nikos Christodoulakis said.

"The convergence is not just nominal but real," Christodoulakis told a conference on the Greek economy. "The character of fiscal policy is not tax-oriented. The 1997 budget is balanced between spending and taxes."
Greece should aim not only to join EMU but also to have a problem-free stay once it gets there, he added.
Fiscal policy will be the only tool available in the hands of the government to fine-tune the economy after Greece becomes a member of EMU, he said.

"There will be tax competition between countries and governments then," said Christodoulakis. "Countries adopting measures that increase the tax burden and not the tax base will be at a disadvantage."
Greece made a sincere effort in reducing spending and evaluating the effectiveness of expenditures but institutional adjustments were also needed to help the economy once it joins EMU, he added.
"The interest expenditures to GDP ratio has come down 1.5 percent compared to 1996, giving an adrenaline shot to new investment initiatives," said Christodoulakis.

Interest expenditures on public debt were being reduced not just in absolute numbers but also relative to GDP by decreasing the cost of borrowing and introducing new management methods to lengthen the maturity of the public debt, he added.
The borrowing rate is at historically low levels and the spread between rates on government securities and savings rates are currently at 0.4 percent from 4.5 percent in December 1991, he said.

"This is a vote of confidence for the government's economic policies," said Christodoulakis. "Nominal rate reductions lately are also catching up with real rate reductions." --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Intercontinental Newsroom +301 9206370
